entity_note: FCG.NZ is the Fonterra Co-operative Group co-operative share itself: voting, held and traded only by supplying/former-supplying farmers on the restricted Fonterra Shareholders' Market. It is distinct from the Fonterra Shareholders' Fund units (FSF.NZ), which are openly tradeable, carry no vote, are capped at ~107m units and trade at a large, persistent premium to FCG. Most outside investors cannot buy FCG.NZ. This valuation is per co-operative share; it is not a valuation of FSF units, whose price embeds a scarcity premium this model does not attempt to explain. Unchanged from the 2026-08-10 build.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 UNDERLYING continuing-operations revenue (pro forma for Mainland trade terms), FY26 results presentation p.41. Replaces the prior 22,267 blended FY24/FY25 base now that a full post-divestment year has printed. Total Group FY26 revenue was 27,432 including eight months of the divested Mainland business. Reconciles to Metrics.csv FY2026 continuing revenue 25,398 (statutory, FY26 AR p.'Revenue from sale of goods') less 158 pro-forma adjustment for post-sale Mainland trade terms (FY26 presentation reconciliation, line 'Revenue from sale of goods' 25,398 -> (158) -> 25,240). Underlying continuing EBIT 1,840 = 7.29% of 25,240 (7.24% of 25,398). Confirmed 2026-09-26 against the financial-parser's FY2026 core_metrics row: base year, net debt and share count already reflected FY26 actuals, so no driver changed on ingestion.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average Co-operative shares FY2026 (1,606.584m, FY26 Annual Report EPS note), i.e. the 1,609.191m on issue at 31-Jul-2026 less ~2.6m treasury shares held by the Custodian for market-making. No dilutive instruments exist (the only LTI is cash-settled). Held flat: the DRP was terminated 2-Sep-2026 and the Fund cap limits issuance; FY26 buyback of $36m was market-maker related.
inputs.net_debt_note: Fonterra ADJUSTED net debt at 31-Jul-2026 = 1,653 (FY26 Annual Report capital-management note): total borrowings 2,847 (incl. 265 lease liabilities) + overdraft 37 - cash 947 - hedge/fair-value adjustments on borrowings. total_debt is shown as 2,600 = 1,653 + 947 so debt - cash ties to the adjusted measure. Replaces the prior ESTIMATE of 2,300 (deseasonalised H1-26 bridge). 31-July is the seasonal low point of the milk-payment cycle; the timing benefit in the FY26 figure is normalised in equity_bridge.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 Total Group OCF 2,651 - PP&E 884 - intangibles 137. NOT the modelling base: it carries a 601 working-capital inflow (supplier-payable timing from the lower advance rate), 692 of cash tax inflated by tax on the Mainland gain, and eight months of Mainland. The engine builds each year from revenue and components instead.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report share-based payment note: $11m expense for the Alignment Rights plan, which is CASH-SETTLED against the Co-operative share price (no share issuance). It is already a cash cost inside operating expenses and hence inside EBITDA, so the explicit SBC row is 0% to avoid charging it twice. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income FY26 was $18m but Fonterra carries net DEBT, so no interest-income strip applies. Net finance costs are NOT deducted in the flows (unlevered flows, net debt deducted once in the bridge).
inputs.wacc_rationale: ONE WACC of 11.0% for all three scenarios (prior build used 12.75% base / 11.25% bull / 14.75% bear with stacked premiums). Built in NZD: NZ 10-yr government ~4.6%, ERP 6.0%, beta 0.9 (dairy commodity processor; the beta carries the systematic milk-price cycle) -> cost of equity ~10.0%; A- rated debt ~5.3% pre-tax / 3.8% after tax; market D/V ~17% (1.65bn adjusted net debt vs ~8.0bn co-op share market cap) -> ~9.0% CAPM WACC. PLUS 2.0% restricted-market illiquidity premium (UNCHANGED from the prior build): FCG shares trade only among eligible farmers on the Fonterra Shareholders' Market, a marketability discount that no scenario flow captures. REMOVED: the prior 1.5% cyclicality premium (now carried by the beta and by the bear case's FY18/19-style margin collapse at 30% weight), the 1.25% China/methane concentration premium and the 0.5% governance residual (both carried in the bear flows and weight). Per the house rule risk is charged once, in the flows, and never by varying WACC across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: the 265 of lease liabilities sits inside adjusted net debt, IFRS-16 EBITDA is used (no lease charge in the flows, lease_cost_pct 0), and right-of-use additions (62 in FY26) are inside the capex path because Fonterra's 'capital invested' guidance of $1.3-1.6bn includes ROU additions. Same treatment as the prior build.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the flows: NCI profit was $40m in FY26 (3.4% of underlying PAT 1,182). Folded into the cash-tax driver: 29% cash tax (underlying FY26 effective 29.4%; Fonterra exhausted its NZ tax losses in FY25 and co-op dividends are no longer deductible) + ~2.5pp NCI leakage = 31.5%. FY0 tie: 1,840 EBIT x (1-0.315) - 166 finance x 0.706 = 1,143 vs reported attributable underlying profit 1,141 (71c x 1,606.6m). NCI equity (84) is NOT also deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), same family as the 2026-08-10 build but now generated by make build-dcf from this Drivers file; the prior was a hand-built 5-year EBIT-margin model. Fonterra post the 31-Mar-2026 Mainland sale is a B2B Ingredients (FY26 EBIT 1,293) and Foodservice (EBIT 547) exporter; it is an operating company with real free cash flow, not a REIT/bank/holdco. Two co-op quirks handled explicitly: (1) the Farmgate Milk Price is the dominant cost and resets each season, so revenue and margins are milk-price driven and modelled mid-cycle; (2) the FSF/FCG entity split (see entity_note). The FY2024 $804m and April-2026 $3.2bn capital returns have both already been paid and are inside the 31-Jul-2026 balance sheet; nothing further is deducted. Horizon extended 5 -> 10 years because the FY27-FY29 capex step-up ($1.3-1.6bn/yr vs ~$0.85bn steady state) means the year-5 FCF margin is not yet mature on a 5-year build. Price is a single NZX print of a thin, farmer-only market; FSF.NZ trades at a large premium and is not a parity check for this security.

equity_bridge.note: FY26 Annual Report balance sheet, current assets; cash still due from Lactalis, not in adjusted net debt and not in the operating flows

FY26 adjusted net debt benefited from a 565 supplier-payable timing inflow (lower milk price and advance-rate reduction, FY26 presentation p.31); working-capital days fell to 84 from 89 (FY23-25). Reversing 5 days on 25.2bn revenue = -345.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-7.7% 3yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+3.7%) and EPS: it is a capital-return artefact (the $804m FY24 and $3,213m FY26 capital returns shrank equity from 8,344 to 6,266), not value destruction. EPS CAGRs use Total Group NORMALISED EPS (FY26 87c includes Mainland; underlying continuing 71c) and the 5-yr figure starts from the FY21 36c trough. None of these series describes the post-divestment business. The DCF uses a through-cycle revenue growth of ~2-2.8% (NZ milk collections are land/environmentally capped; growth is milk-price inflation plus mix), UNCHANGED from the prior build.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are Total Group (FY26 27,432 vs FY23 24,580 / FY21 20,565). FCF CAGRs are not reported: FY22 FCF was negative and FY26 Total Group FCF (1,630 ex-divestment proceeds) carries a 601 working-capital timing inflow and tax on the Mainland gain. SBC is nil (cash-settled plan), so owner FCF = reported FCF and there is no SBC-driven divergence. CSV-basis cross-check (Metrics.csv FY2026 row is CONTINUING revenue 25,398, earlier rows Total Group): 3yr 1.1%, 5yr 4.3% -- mixed basis, understated by the Mainland exclusion; the Total Group CAGRs above remain the like-for-like measure. Metrics.csv FY2026 net income 2,608 / EPS $1.60 are statutory and include the 1,262 discontinued result (Mainland gain); the DCF uses underlying continuing (EBIT 1,840, EPS ~71c), never statutory.

base.growth_rates_note: Y1 (FY27) 0.5%: forecast milk price $9.50 vs $9.69 (-2%) against collections 'just above 1.6bn kgMS' vs 1,571m (+2%). Y2-Y5 2.8/2.6/2.4/2.2 UNCHANGED from the prior build; Y6-Y10 at the 2.0% terminal rate (new years from the horizon extension).
base.ebitda_margin_note: EBIT margin path 7.4 / 7.0 / 6.7 / 6.5 / 6.3 then 6.3 flat, plus D&A. Y1 7.4% = FY27 EPS guidance midpoint (75c: 1,877 EBIT - ~130 finance, 29% tax, 40 NCI). Mid-cycle RAISED from 5.6% to 6.3%: the clean post-divestment underlying series is now FY25 6.2% (at a peak $10.16 milk price, which squeezes processor margins) and FY26 7.3%, with FY27 guided ~7.4%. The prior 5.3-5.6% mid-cycle was anchored on pre-divestment Total Group history (FY18/19 losses were largely in now-divested Consumer/China farms/Beingmate assets). 6.3% gives back most of the FY26-27 strength and assumes the ~$3bn FY27-29 programme earns no margin uplift.
base.da_note: FY26 continuing D&A 525 = 2.1% of revenue; rises to 2.6% as the FY27-29 capex programme (~$1.45bn/yr) is commissioned. Prior used 2.3% flat.
base.capex_note: FY27-FY29 guided $1.3-1.6bn/yr capital invested (midpoint 1.45bn = 5.7% of revenue), including the incremental ~$1bn South Island protein network, $100-300m/yr energy and wastewater, ~$600-700m/yr sustaining. Prior build had 2.8% -> 2.4%, which the new guidance overturns. Steady state 3.3% (~$1bn at FY36 revenue) vs 2.6% D&A: sustaining ~700 in FY26 dollars plus ongoing decarbonisation spend.
base.tax_note: 29% cash tax (FY26 underlying effective 29.4%; NZ tax losses exhausted FY25, co-op dividends no longer deductible) + 2.5pp NCI leakage. Prior: 27% + 4% NCI (~29.9% combined).
base.wc_note: Manufacturer/exporter: growth consumes working capital. -15% of the revenue CHANGE (average net WC ~84-89 days on a seasonal cycle, partly funded by the farmer payable). Prior used a 20% use (equivalent to -20); lowered because the milk-payment schedule structurally finances part of inventory.
base.narrative: Base: Fonterra runs as a focused B2B processor. FY27 lands on the 65-85c guidance midpoint, then margins mean-revert from the FY26-27 strength to a 6.3% EBIT mid-cycle, above the pre-divestment Total Group history because the loss-making Consumer, China farms and Beingmate assets are gone. Revenue follows milk-price inflation with capped NZ volumes. FY27-29 capex of ~$1.45bn/yr depresses FCF to ~$0.2-0.4bn for three years and earns only enough to hold margins, not lift them.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: EBIT 7.8% FY27 (upper half of guidance, ~80c) held at ~7.5% mid-cycle as protein and Foodservice mix lifts: Foodservice already earns 11.2% EBIT (FY26) and grows faster than Ingredients (6.4%). Prior bull ran 5.8% -> 6.8% EBIT on the pre-divestment base; raised for the same reason as base.
bull.narrative: Bull: the South Island protein network and Studholme move milk out of whole milk powder into advanced proteins; Foodservice (11% EBIT) grows in Greater China and Southeast Asia; the ERP programme lowers cost per kgMS. EBIT margin holds ~7.5-7.8% through the cycle and revenue grows 3-4% on value mix. Terminal growth 2.5% and cap 14x, unchanged from the prior bull.

bear.growth_rates_note: Y1 -1.0% (milk price toward the $8.50 low end); Y2-Y5 -1.0/0.5/1.0/1.2 UNCHANGED from the prior bear; 1.5% thereafter (= prior bear terminal growth).
bear.ebitda_margin_note: EBIT 6.6% FY27 (guidance low end, ~65c), then an FY18/19-style collapse to 3.0% in FY28 (GDT slump plus China import decline plus stranded new capacity), recovering to 4.5% mid-cycle. Prior bear: 3.5 / 1.5 / 3.0 / 3.8 / 4.0; trough and steady state lifted ~0.5pp because the Consumer losses that drove FY18/19 are divested, but the shape is retained.
bear.capex_note: Programme partly deferred in a downturn: 5.5 / 4.8 / 4.3% then 3.0%.
bear.narrative: Bear: global milk supply (US, EU) keeps GDT prices weak while China's self-sufficiency cuts whole-milk-powder imports; methane pricing starts to shrink the NZ milk pool; a new CEO commits ~$3bn of capex into a downturn and the new protein capacity earns below its cost of capital. Margins repeat an FY18/19-style trough and settle at 4.5% EBIT.

scenario_narratives.base: Fonterra runs as a focused B2B processor. FY27 lands on the 65-85c guidance midpoint (EBIT ~7.4%), then margins mean-revert to a 6.3% EBIT mid-cycle, above pre-divestment history because the loss-making Consumer, China farms and Beingmate assets are gone, and below FY26-27. Revenue follows milk-price inflation on capped NZ volumes (~2-2.8%/yr). The FY27-29 capex programme (~$1.45bn/yr) holds FCF to ~$0.2-0.4bn a year and earns only enough to defend margins.
scenario_narratives.bull: Protein and Foodservice mix shift works: the South Island protein network and Studholme move milk out of commodity powders into advanced proteins, Foodservice (11.2% EBIT in FY26) keeps compounding in Greater China and Southeast Asia, and the ERP roll-out lowers cost per kgMS. EBIT holds ~7.5-7.8% through the cycle with 3-4% revenue growth; 2.5% terminal growth, 14x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: GDT weakness from surging US/EU milk supply and China's rising self-sufficiency produce an FY18/19-style trough (EBIT 3% in FY28) just as ~$3bn of new capacity is commissioned under a new CEO; NZ methane pricing starts to shrink the milk pool. Margins settle at 4.5% EBIT, revenue grows ~1-1.5%, terminal growth 1.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from the prior build. Bear 30% (above the 15% default): a dairy commodity processor with two loss-adjacent years in the last nine, a milk-price forecast that moved $9.75 -> $9.25 -> $9.50 in four months, and a capex step-up committed at a cyclical high; this weight now carries the cyclicality and China-concentration risk that the prior build also charged through WACC premiums. Base 50%: FY26 delivered at the top of guidance and FY27 guidance brackets the base. Bull 20% (below the 35% default): the bull needs mix shift, Foodservice growth and capex returns to all go right at once.
probability_weighted.evidence_that_would_move_weights: Two consecutive GDT auctions that pull the 2026/27 milk price forecast below $9.00 or an FY27 guidance cut to below 65c -> bear up. H1-FY27 EBIT margin above 7.5% with Foodservice volume growth above 5% -> bull up.

valuation_philosophy.summary: FCG.NZ is valued per Fonterra co-operative share on continuing (post-Mainland) operations only: an unlevered, mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF over 10 years with the adjusted net debt at 31-Jul-2026 deducted once. The Mainland proceeds and the $3.2bn capital return are already inside that balance sheet. The value is dominated by two judgments: the mid-cycle EBIT margin (6.3% base) and the 2% restricted-market premium in an 11% WACC. The FY27-29 capex programme holds near-term owner FCF well below earnings, so P/E comparisons flatter the stock relative to cash returns.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_growth_dcf: Fonterra is a cyclical commodity processor, not a compounder: NZ milk collections are structurally capped, revenue growth is essentially milk-price inflation, and margins swing with the Global Dairy Trade cycle. The base therefore mean-reverts margins rather than extrapolating FY26-27.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: each 0.5pp of steady-state EBIT margin is worth roughly $0.65-0.70 per share (about 100m/yr of after-tax FCF capitalised at 11% less 2% growth)
Capex returns: ~$4.3bn over FY27-29 is modelled to hold margins, not lift them; if it earns nothing the base is too high, if it earns the cost of capital the bull's mix story applies
Restricted-market illiquidity premium (2%): removing it takes WACC to ~9% and lifts value materially; it is a judgment about the farmer-only market, not about the business
Milk price and GDT volatility: FY27 guidance spans 65-85c on only two months of the season
Price reference: the NZX print for FCG is a thin farmer-only market and diverges widely from FSF.NZ; upside/downside against it is less informative than for a liquid security
valuation_philosophy.unchanged_judgments: Deliberately left alone: entity framing (FCG vs FSF), probability weights 30/50/20, base growth Y2-Y5 (2.8/2.6/2.4/2.2), bear growth Y2-Y5, terminal growth (2.0 / 2.5 / 1.5), terminal caps (13 / 14 / 13), the 2.0% restricted-market illiquidity premium, lease treatment (A), SBC nil. Evidence that would move them: a board decision on the Fund cap or a farmer-only Fund market (illiquidity premium and entity framing); a structural change in NZ milk supply from methane pricing (growth); a sustained GDT regime shift (terminal growth).

prior_version.note: Prior was a hand-built 5-year EBIT-margin model with per-scenario WACC (12.75 / 11.25 / 14.75), net finance costs deducted inside the flows AND net debt deducted in the bridge, and a 2,300 ESTIMATED net debt. Price refreshed to 5.00 on 2026-08-12 without a rebuild.

bridge.item: Methodology: prior drivers re-run through make build-dcf -- net finance costs no longer deducted in the flows while net debt is also deducted (interest double-count removed), NCI 4% folded into cash tax, working capital as a use on revenue change

Methodology: one 11.0% WACC for all scenarios replaces 12.75/11.25/14.75 (cyclicality, concentration and governance premiums removed; risk now charged once, in the bear flows and 30% weight; 2.0% restricted-market premium kept)

Anchor refresh: FY26 actual underlying revenue 25,240 as FY0 (vs 22,267 blended base), adjusted net debt 1,653 at 31-Jul-2026 (vs 2,300 estimate), equity bridge -185 (Mainland receivable +160, WC timing -345), shares 1,606.6m (ex-treasury)
Methodology: horizon 5 -> 10 years (prior paths extended at their last value)

Driver changes from FY26 results/FY27 guidance: capex to $1.3-1.6bn/yr FY27-29 then 3.3% (was 2.8->2.4%), D&A 2.1->2.6%, cash tax+NCI 31.5% (was ~29.9%), mid-cycle EBIT raised 5.6->6.3% base (bull ~7.5%, bear 4.5%), FY27 at guidance midpoint, WC use 20->15%
Price move since the prior build (no effect on IV; upside changes only -- see prior_version.price_then and current_price)
